body.x: A stopped machine costs a plant production time, and the maintenance team often learns about a fault only after the line has gone down. The data that could have flagged it usually sits in SCADA, MES and monitoring systems that are separate from the tools technicians use to plan and carry out repairs.

ManWinWin Software, a Portuguese provider of computerized maintenance management systems (CMMS) and enterprise asset management (EAM) with more than 40 years of experience, is led by General Manager and Partner Rodrigo Seruya Cabral. At KES 2026, the company is presenting its enterprise CMMS platform, which includes AI-powered maintenance analytics, mobile work order execution and OT and IT integration, and is looking for South Korean industrial automation system integrators as channel partners.

Instead of replacing existing SCADA, MES or industrial IoT infrastructure, ManWinWin ingests real-time machine alarms and run-hours and uses them to trigger work requests, condition inspections or work orders, with a human kept in the loop for operational control. The platform manages work orders, preventive maintenance schedules, spare parts inventory and equipment lifecycle costs, and offers mobile apps for shop-floor technicians and KPI analytics. The company says it cuts unplanned downtime by up to 18%, eliminates roughly 20% of reactive maintenance tasks and recovers 8% of technician wrench-time, with payback within 12 to 18 months.

ManWinWin says it serves manufacturing, energy and process facilities in more than 100 countries, and that more than 70% of its business comes from long-term recurring relationships. South Korea's CS WIND uses it in plants in Denmark and Portugal and is extending it to its U.S. facilities in Colorado. The company also lists Petronas in Malaysia, Unilever in Indonesia and Watsons in the Philippines as Asian references. The software is ISO 9001 certified, with ISO 27001 certification under way, and supports more than 20 languages.

The company is targeting South Korea's high-tech manufacturing sector, where smart factory adoption is rising. It wants to reach two types of partners: automation integrators specializing in SCADA, MES or web control systems, and engineering and plant operation and maintenance providers. It also plans to offer CMMS digitalization directly to Tier 2 and Tier 3 manufacturers in semiconductors, EV batteries and precision machinery. After KES 2026, it plans to strengthen regional technical support and partner training across Asia-Pacific. Building brand awareness among plant decision-makers is its main challenge in Korea.

KES 2026, the 57th Korea Electronics Show, runs Oct. 13 to Oct. 16 at COEX Halls A and B in Seoul. Alongside the co-located XR & Spatial Computing Show, the event features X-SPACE 2026, a special exhibition covering digital twins, industrial XR, spatial intelligence, XR devices and spatial computing platforms. The Innovation Awards ceremony takes place on Oct. 13.
